title: How to Plan a UGC Video Campaign Before Hiring Creators
h1: How to plan a UGC video campaign before hiring creators
description: Plan a UGC video campaign: goal, product shipping, creator profile, hooks, brief, usage rights, testing, disclosure rules and what to ask creators.
intro: User-generated-style content, often called UGC, means short videos made by real-looking people who show or talk about your product in a natural way. Brands use them in ads, on product pages and on social media because they feel more genuine than polished commercials. A good campaign needs a plan: who the videos are for, what they should say, how you will use them and what rights you need. This article explains how to prepare before hiring creators.

faq.q: How many videos should I order first?
faq.a: A small batch with different hooks and creators is common, so you can see what your audience responds to before ordering more.
Usually yes. Plan shipping, timing and what happens to the product afterward.

faq.q: What usage rights should I request?
faq.a: State whether the videos are for organic posts, paid ads or both, for how long and on which platforms, and get this in writing.

faq.q: Do creators have to disclose a connection to my brand?
faq.a: Rules in many places require clear disclosure when content is paid or promotional. Ask creators and check the rules that apply to you.
Ask for raw footage or permission to trim and add captions, since many campaigns need several cuts.
